card.name: The word initial before a transient effect
card.fires_on: The word "initial" (or a comma or small word just before one) when a drug effect is described as starting one way before reversing, such as an initial rise or initial tachycardia.

modes.label: Initial before an effect
modes.description: The word "initial" right before a first-phase effect like tachycardia or a rise in blood glucose.

modes.label: Comma before initially
modes.description: A comma after a drug class name, where the next word is likely "initially".
modes.example: SUPPRELIN LA, like other GnRH agonists<<,>> initially causes a transient increase in serum concentrations

modes.label: Small words before symptom lists
modes.description: Small words such as "by" or "an" just before a list of early symptoms.
